LLM_description:
Situation:
A severe weather system has disrupted ground lines of communication across the province. Flooded lowlands, landslide-prone valleys, and damaged bridges are constraining movement. Multiple forward elements—coastal, highland, and urban—require immediate resupply of water, rations, and medical materiel. Regional stocks are positioned at Supply Depot Alpha, Supply Depot Bravo, Supply Depot Charlie, and Supply Depot Delta. Movement windows are variable and some corridors require engineer clearance and armed escort due to sporadic civil unrest and debris hazards.

Mission:
Deliver priority relief commodities to all designated forward units within the current operational window while minimizing total cost, balancing transport expenditures, fixed route security overhead, vehicle deployment costs, and acceptable shortage penalties.

Execution/Concept:
- Supply availability: Outbound allocations from each depot are constrained by on-hand stocks by supply class and by day. Replenishment variability means not all depots can support all commodities each day.
- Demand fulfillment: Each receiving unit has daily minimum requirements by supply class. Controlled shortfalls are permitted only when operationally unavoidable and will incur shortage penalties to reflect unmet needs.
- Transport and loading: Movements follow predefined depot-to-unit corridors. Transport costs are route- and day-dependent. Vehicles can consolidate multiple supply classes per run, subject to per-vehicle volumetric capacity limits defined by the supply types.
- Fleet and deployment: Vehicles are discrete assets with a per-vehicle deployment cost. The total number of vehicles deployed on any day cannot exceed the available fleet. Convoy assignment to any corridor is not permitted unless the corridor is activated.
- Route activation and risk: Activating a corridor—sending any vehicles on that route on a given day—incurs a fixed Risk Cost for security overhead (escort teams, route clearance, coordination), regardless of the number of vehicles dispatched on that corridor that day. This fixed cost applies once per activated route per day and is in addition to per-vehicle transport costs.
- Prioritization: Emphasize life-sustaining commodities and medically critical items. Use consolidation at depots with stronger stock positions, align dispatch with anticipated clearance windows, and limit the number of activated corridors unless the combined effect of transport and risk costs justifies additional routes.
- Command and support: The Logistics Coordination Cell will synchronize engineer and security support for corridor activation and allocate fleet assets across depots to meet critical demands first while maintaining operational flexibility across the planning horizon.
